news.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
news.summary_raw: Introducing private, server-side memory to Private AI Compute for personal AI.

news.title: How to Use NVIDIA Warp and MjWarp to Accelerate Robotics Simulation and Learning Workflows
news.summary: NVIDIA has launched Warp and MjWarp, SDKs that integrate with NVIDIA Isaac Sim and MuJoCo to enable faster, more efficient robotics simulation and learning workflows. These tools lower GPU memory usage and reduce simulation time, allowing developers to train models more quickly.

news.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
news.summary_raw:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.
The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has demonstrated that offloading AI inference from robot hardware to external processors can improve task success rates and operational efficiency. The findings suggest that distributed inference architectures could enable more complex physical AI workloads.
news.enterprise_use: Watch for potential API or SDK releases from Microsoft that facilitate offloading inference to Azure services or edge devices. Evaluate how this could integrate with your existing MDM or endpoint security frameworks by enabling robots to run heavy models on cloud servers while maintaining local control.

news.summary_raw:

news.summary: Microsoft Research has introduced RetroChimera, a predictive model that improves small‑molecule synthesis planning at scale. The model enables faster, more cost‑effective exploration of chemical spaces, potentially accelerating drug and material discovery.
news.enterprise_use: Check the RetroChimera API documentation on Microsoft Research’s website and evaluate whether integrating its predictions could reduce synthetic route planning time in your R&D workflows. This will help you assess whether the model could replace or supplement existing cheminformatics tools, improving efficiency in experimental design.
